D.t: Peggy Flanagan leads by 11.3 in the forecast and wins 98% of simulations. The cushion is about 315,810 votes; a one point swing is about 13,999 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +4.5 and D +18.1. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +8.3. Your best recent poll is New York Times/Siena at D +13.3; your worst is InsiderAdvantage at D +1.1. 12 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Hennepin, a projected net 336,592 votes; Ramsey, a projected net 137,235 votes; Dakota, a projected net 40,203 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Anoka, D +1.6, 6.3% of the vote; Scott, R +6.5, 2.7% of the vote; Carver, R +6.5, 2.1% of the vote; Rice, D +2.4, 1.1% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Peggy Flanagan runs furthest behind in Carver, Wright, Crow Wing. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 87% of voters, 51 to 46, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.36 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 75% of voters, 54 to 43, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.75 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 58% of voters, 55 to 42, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.90 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Peggy Flanagan: Immigration voters 25 to 73, Small counties 36 to 61, Midsize counties 48 to 50. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$1.1M cash against $1.4M. Roughly even money; the air war will be decided by outside groups and earned media.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.1 points away from Peggy Flanagan. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.
Activity: 3 campaign stops by the candidate or surrogates in 30 days.

R.t: Michele Tafoya trails by 11.3 and wins 2% of simulations. Closing it takes about 157,905 voters switching sides, or 315,810 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +18.1 and D +4.5. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +8.3. Your best recent poll is InsiderAdvantage at D +1.1; your worst is New York Times/Siena at D +13.3. 12 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Wright, a projected net 21,538 votes; Stearns, a projected net 17,133 votes; Sherburne, a projected net 16,058 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Anoka, D +1.6, 6.3% of the vote; Scott, R +6.5, 2.7% of the vote; Carver, R +6.5, 2.1% of the vote; Rice, D +2.4, 1.1% of the vote.

R.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Michele Tafoya runs furthest behind in St. Louis, Ramsey, Hennepin. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 87% of voters, 46 to 51, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.36 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 75% of voters, 43 to 54, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.75 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 58% of voters, 42 to 55, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.90 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Michele Tafoya: Black voters 16 to 81, Asian and other voters 26 to 72, Large counties 29 to 69. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$1.4M cash against $1.1M. Roughly even money; the air war will be decided by outside groups and earned media.

R.h: What the ballots so far say
R.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.1 points toward Michele Tafoya. Bank it: chase the remaining mail ballots and low propensity voters who have not voted.
